assumptions: A shared-axis fold is a proposed metaphor for observation, not a simulation of an exercise or a measured audience response.
brief.audience: People training with motion tracking and a 3D exercise model.
brief.name: Reprism

philosophies.statement: Make movement understandable without visual noise.
Observe the same underlying movement consistently.
Read one movement through different views and notice its differences.

brief.purpose: Help people observe, understand, and replay their exercise motion.

rules.statement: Both faces must derive from the same geometric R source.
Use equal stem and perpendicular diagonal weight in the source plane; projected weights may foreshorten.
The orthographic fold projection must preserve every point on the shared axis.
Use an actual seam between projected faces, with nominal clearance above 1px at a 28px wordmark height.

brief.typography: Outlined Manrope at weight 700; a project choice rather than a generic default.

rationale.check: Verify fixed points and normal foreshortening of the projection; inspect the silhouette.
rationale.observable_result: The upper counter and rim change with the view while the lower face remains stable.
rationale.rule: Use front and folded projections of exactly the same source across a fixed axis.

rationale.check: Both faces must derive from source and affine_transform(source,matrix).
rationale.observable_result: One recognizable R with related faces.
rationale.rule: Reuse the complete geometric source for both observations rather than drawing a second unrelated glyph.

rationale.check: Exactly two valid faces; nominal clearance above 1px at 28px, followed by browser review.
rationale.observable_result: The folded relationship survives single-color reproduction at header sizes.
rationale.rule: Separate views with a controlled negative seam and preserve a readable counter.
